Nur für den Admin, höchstens 60 Abfragen pro Minute. Gefiltert wird in Python mit einer festen Liste; an journalctl gehen nur Zahlen aus festen Listen. Bot-Tokens, Bearer-Schlüssel, password=/token=/key=-Werte und Zugangsdaten in Adressen werden vor der Anzeige geschwärzt.

head: Logs
title: Logs-Seite „Überblick zuerst“
text: Logs-Seite „Überblick zuerst“ (ab V01.0.212): Reiter Diagnose, Dienste, Update und Änderungen. Unter Diagnose zeigen Kacheln die Fehlerzahl und die drei lebhaftesten Bereiche mit kleinem Verlauf über den Zeitraum (Antippen filtert), darunter der letzte Fehler mit einem festen Hinweis (z. B. HTTP 401 bei Home Assistant → Token abgelaufen). Filterknöpfe mit Trefferzahl: Gespräch, Websuche, Weiche, Home Assistant, Raum, Lautsprecher, Telegram, Mail und „Nur Fehler“. Jede Zeile zeigt Uhrzeit, Bereich und Meldung; Fehler rot, Warnungen gelb (feste Wortliste im Panel), gleiche Zeilen als „×n“, Pausen ab 2 min als Trennlinie. Die Suche läuft nur im Browser über die geladenen Zeilen. „Live“ lädt alle 10 s (Dienste alle 3 s) und pausiert, solange man hochscrollt oder etwas markiert. „Kopieren für Thread“ nimmt Version, Filter und die Rohzeilen im Code-Block mit.

head: Logs
title: Telegram: nur ein Abruf
text: Telegram: nur ein Abruf (ab V01.0.214): Telegram gibt neue Nachrichten immer nur an einen Abruf (getUpdates) gleichzeitig. Bis V01.0.213 liefen die Startaufgaben des Panels doppelt (der https-Server führte sie ein zweites Mal aus), und die zwei Telegram-Abrufe warfen sich alle 15 s gegenseitig raus („Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request“). Jetzt startet der https-Server ohne eigene Startaufgaben, und ein zweiter Abruf im selben Prozess wird nicht gestartet. Meldet Telegram trotzdem einen Konflikt, nutzt ein anderes Programm denselben Bot-Token: Der Spark wartet dann 5 s, 30 s, 1, 2, 5 und höchstens 10 min, schreibt nur die zweite und jede 20. Meldung ins Log (ohne Token) und zeigt unter Zustand und bei Einbinden → Telegram den Hinweis, den Token nur an einer Stelle zu nutzen oder bei @BotFather einen neuen zu holen. Ein einzelner Konflikt direkt nach einem Neustart ist normal (der alte Abruf läuft noch bis zu 25 s).

head: Logs
title: Wetterdienst kurz weg
text: Wetterdienst kurz weg (ab V01.0.214): Antwortet Open-Meteo für die Wetternotiz mit 5xx oder 429 oder gar nicht, steht im Log eine Warnung („retry in 10 min“) statt eines Fehlers, und der Spark versucht es innerhalb des Zeitfensters alle 10 min wieder.

head: Logs
title: Webanfragen in den Logs
text: Webanfragen in den Logs (ab V01.0.215): Bei Zeilen des Webservers („GET /api/… 200 OK“) entscheidet nur der Statuscode über Rot (ab 500), nie Wörter in der Adresse. Die Abrufe der Logs-Seite selbst schreibt das Panel gar nicht mehr ins Journal. Zeilen des Updates, die einen Versionstext zitieren („Available: 46fb0e8 …“, „Update finished: …“), bekommen keine Farbe (ab V01.0.216). Die Zeitangabe darf „+0200“, „+02:00“ oder „Z“ sein (ab V01.0.217; vorher blieben bei „+02:00“ alle Bereiche auf 0).

head: Logs
title: Ausführliche Diagnose pro Bereich
text: Ausführliche Diagnose pro Bereich (Logs → Erweitert): Raum-Modus, Lautsprecher, Home Assistant und Gespräch lassen sich für 15 min, 1 h oder 4 h einschalten; danach und bei jedem Neustart sind sie wieder aus. Sie schreiben zusätzliche … detail …-Zeilen nur mit Zahlen und Entscheidungen (Erkennungszeit, Antwortzeit, Wortzahl, Dauer eines Home-Assistant-Aufrufs, Größe des Verlaufs, angebotene Werkzeuge), nie gehörte oder geschriebene Texte, Namen oder Geheimnisse; die Schwärzung läuft trotzdem. Nur für den Admin, mit Rate-Limit.

head: Was installiert wird
title: Was installiert wird
text: Alle Dienste laufen als Systembenutzer speech. Per sudoers darf das Panel die Speech-Dienste und Engines starten, stoppen und neu starten und das Update anstoßen, sonst nichts.

head: Leistung messen
title: Leistung messen
text: Im Panel unter Zustand → Prüfen → Leistung messen oder auf der Konsole:

head: Leistung messen
title: Leistung messen
text: Seit V01.0.163 bekommt jeder Wert eine Stufe (sehr gut, gut, knapp, zu langsam) und einen Satz, ab wann er gut ist; oben steht ein Gesamturteil, und neben dem Wert die letzte Messung. Die Grenzen sind feste Regeln in bench.rate():

head: Leistung messen
title: Leistung messen
text: „Richtig verstanden“ fehlt bei --audio, weil der Text der eigenen Aufnahme unbekannt ist. Die Kennzahlen der letzten zehn Messungen stehen in bench-history.json.

head: Leistung messen
title: Leistung messen
text: Die Messung geht über die öffentlichen Ports, misst also das, was Apps sehen. Das letzte Ergebnis steht in /var/lib/speech-spark/state/bench-latest.json. Die Speicheranteile der Engines (Konfiguration) sind Startwerte: nach der Messung passend einstellen.

head: Neben dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Neben dgx-spark-qwen38
text: - Ports: qwen38 nutzt 30000 bis 30099 (Engine 30000, Proxy 30001, Bild 30020, Video 30022, Cockpit 30090/30091). Speech nutzt 31001, 31002, 31080 und 31443 (Panel über https); die Engines auf 31011, 31012 und 31013 hören nur auf 127.0.0.1. Das Panel lehnt Ports im Bereich von qwen38 ab, und das Installationsskript bricht ab, wenn ein Port schon belegt ist. - Speicher: Die GB10 hat einen gemeinsamen Pool von 128 GB für CPU und GPU. Die qwen38-Lanes reservieren davon einen festen Anteil: 50 % bei stock/fp8, 76 % im 1M-Modus und 85 % bei flash. Laut qwen38-Doku bleiben bei flash im Leerlauf nur ~16,6 GiB frei, und unter ~8 GiB beendet earlyoom von DGX OS Prozesse. Deshalb gilt: - Erkennt das Skript eine flash- oder 1M-Lane, wählt es automatisch die 0.6B-Modelle. - Bevor ein Dienst sein Modell lädt, prüft er, ob danach noch die Reserve frei bleibt (Standard 10 GiB). Wenn nicht, lädt er nicht und zeigt im Panel blocked mit Begründung. - Wird der Speicher trotzdem knapp, beendet das System zuerst das Panel (OOMScoreAdjust=900), dann die Speech-Dienste (500), nicht die LLM-Lane und nicht sshd (siehe „Vorrang für Sprache“). - Speech startet nach den qwen38-Lanes, damit diese ihren festen A

head: Neben dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Neben dgx-spark-qwen38
text: nteil zuerst belegen. - Die Engines starten nacheinander, weil vLLM beim Start den freien Speicher misst und parallele Starts sich gegenseitig den Anteil wegnehmen. - Lane-Wechsel: Wechselst du im Cockpit auf flash, bleiben die schon geladenen Speech-Modelle im Speicher. Mit 1.7B-Modellen kann das zu knapp werden. Dann vorher ASR und TTS im Panel stoppen oder auf 0.6B umstellen. - GPU-Zeit: ASR und TTS teilen sich die GPU mit dem LLM. Während einer Transkription oder Sprachausgabe wird das LLM etwas langsamer.

head: Vorrang für Sprache
title: Vorrang für Sprache
text: Spracherkennung und Sprachausgabe gehen immer vor (feste Regel ohne Schalter, seit V01.0.225, Plan plaene/vorrang-sprache.md).

head: Vorrang für Sprache
title: Vorrang für Sprache
text: - Wann gilt „es wird gesprochen“: während eine Antwort von /api/chat läuft (Browser, App, Lautsprecher, Telegram, Siri) und während ASR oder TTS eine Anfrage bearbeiten, egal von wem (auch Open WebUI und Wyoming). Die Dienste melden das über common.SpeechMark: jede POST /v1/audio/...-Anfrage, die Größenlimit und API-Schlüssel passiert hat, berührt state/speech-active. Danach gilt noch 20 Sekunden als Gespräch (Rückfrage). - Hintergrundarbeit wartet in der Zeit, und ihre laufende Anfrage an das Sprachmodell wird abgebrochen (vLLM beendet sie, sobald die Verbindung zu ist) und in der nächsten Pause wiederholt, höchstens dreimal. Es läuft immer nur eine Hintergrund-Anfrage gleichzeitig. Angeschlossen: Lernen aus Gesprächen, Gedächtnis aufräumen, Agenten, proaktive Hinweise, Tagesüberblick, Mail sortieren, Qualitätstest, Dokumente lesen und Bedeutungssuche (wissen.quiet()), Sicherung (läuft zusätzlich mit niedriger CPU-Priorität). - Neuer Hinweis in health.alerts: auch in live.hints eintragen, mit Ort im Bild und festen Worten. - Neues Ereignis im Admin-Protokoll (guard.log): ein festes Wort in guard.LIVE_WORDS, dann steht es unter Ereignisse. Eine Zeile von irgendwo: live.mark(bereich

head: Vorrang für Sprache
title: Vorrang für Sprache
text: , text); etwas, das der Spark selbst mit einem Dienst tut: live.job(warum, werkzeug, t0, ok). - Schnittstelle für neue Hintergrundarbeit (app/panel/vorrang.py): - r = await vorrang.post(c, "Name", url, json=..., headers=...): eine Anfrage an das Sprachmodell (httpx-Client c), wartet, läuft allein, wird bei Sprache abgebrochen und wiederholt; gibt nach drei Abbrüchen mit vorrang.Busy auf. - await vorrang.run("Name", lambda: coroutine()): dasselbe für jede andere Coroutine. - await vorrang.quiet("Name"): nur auf eine Pause warten. - await vorrang.in_thread("Name", fn, *args): CPU-Arbeit (z. B. Einbettungsmodell) nach einer Pause in einem eigenen Thread mit nice 15. - vorrang.hold("Name"): in einem Worker-Thread zwischen zwei Schritten warten, solange gesprochen wird (nie im Event-Loop aufrufen). - vorrang.speaking(): ob gerade gesprochen wird. - Betriebssystem: ASR- und TTS-Dienste und ihre Engines laufen mit Nice=-5, CPUWeight=1000, IOWeight=1000. Bei Speichernot beendet das System zuerst das Panel (OOMScoreAdjust=900), dann die Sprachdienste (500), nicht die LLM-Lane und nicht sshd. - GPU: Prioritäten zwischen Prozessen gibt es auf der GB10 nicht. Der Speicher der Sprach-Engines is

head: Vorrang für Sprache
title: Vorrang für Sprache
text: t ab dem Start fest reserviert. Die eigene Antwort des Sprachmodells läuft gleichzeitig mit der Sprachausgabe; das bremst sie manchmal („tts behind … inside the piece“). - Prüfen: Zustand → Prüfen → „Vorrang für Sprache“ spricht einen Satz alleine, unter Last ohne Vorfahrt und unter Last mit Vorfahrt und zeigt erster Ton, Echtzeitfaktor und Erkennungszeit; darüber die Zähler von heute. In Zustand → Logs stehen die Zeilen im Bereich „Vorrang“ (vorrang: … wartet, … abgebrochen, … wartete N s).

head: Vorrang für Personen
title: Vorrang für Personen
text: Reden mehrere Personen gleichzeitig, bekommen ausgewählte Profile ihre Antwort zuerst (seit V01.0.282, Plan plaene/vorrang-personen.md). Standardmäßig aus.

head: Vorrang für Personen
title: Vorrang für Personen
text: - Einschalten: Funktionen → Gespräch → „Vorrang für Personen“ (chat.person_priority, Funktionsregister vorrang). Die Stufe pro Profil setzt nur der Admin unter Personen und Geräte → Profil → Rechte → Vorrang: „Vorrang“ (höchstens drei Profile), „normal“ oder „hinten anstellen“. Gespeichert in state/personen-vorrang.json (in der Sicherung), Änderungen im Admin-Protokoll (person_priority). Unter Ich sieht das Profil „Vorrang für Personen“ als an oder „bei dir aus“. - Wer fragt: nur aus der Anmeldung (Browser, App, Geräteschlüssel), nie aus dem Text. Gäste und Programme ohne Profil (Open WebUI, Wyoming) sind immer normal. Am geteilten Lautsprecher zählt die Stufe nur, wenn die Sprechererkennung die Stimme des Profils erkannt hat; die Aufnahme selbst geht dort normal in die Erkennung, weil die Stimme erst danach feststeht. - Sprachausgabe und Spracherkennung: Beide Dienste lassen nur so viele Anfragen gleichzeitig zur Engine, wie sie annimmt (tts.engine_max_seqs, asr.engine_max_seqs), der Rest wartet im Dienst (common.PrioGate) nach Stufe, dann nach Eingang. Eine laufende Anfrage wird nie abgebrochen. Wer 4 s wartet, rückt eine Stufe hoch, damit niemand verhungert. Höchstens 64 warten,

head: Vorrang für Personen
title: Vorrang für Personen
text: sonst 503. Ein Platz kommt spätestens nach 90 s zurück, auch wenn ein Gerät die Verbindung vor dem Start fallen ließ. - Sprachmodell (seit V01.0.284): Solange eine Antwort mit Vorrang ihren ersten Satz noch nicht hat, warten neue Runden anderer Personen höchstens chat.person_priority_wait Sekunden (0–5, Standard 2), bevor sie ans Sprachmodell gehen (stufe.wait_turn). Laufende Antworten werden nie abgebrochen, eine Antwort ohne ersten Satz hält andere höchstens 30 s auf. Logs → Anfragen zeigt bei der Runde „wartete … auf eine Antwort mit Vorrang“, Journal vorrang: Antwort wartete N s auf eine Antwort mit Vorrang. - Früher Bescheid: Browser und iPhone-App melden beim Start einer Aufnahme POST /api/vorrang/spricht (Profil oder Geräteschlüssel, höchstens 60 pro Minute). Hat das Profil Vorrang, stoppt die Hintergrundarbeit sofort und das Tor fürs Sprachmodell schließt für höchstens 15 s, bis die Frage da ist. Die Antwort ist für alle gleich, so verrät sie nicht, wer Vorrang hat. Am geteilten Lautsprecher gibt es diesen Bescheid nicht. - Wer die Stufe sagen darf: nur das Panel. Es schickt X-Spark-Stufe (0, 1, 2) zusammen mit dem Schlüssel aus state/vorrang-key (vom Panel einmal erzeugt,

head: Vorrang für Personen
title: Vorrang für Personen
text: Rechte 0600, nicht in der Sicherung). Die Dienste glauben das nur von 127.0.0.1 und nur mit diesem Schlüssel; alle anderen sind normal, auch mit dem API-Schlüssel. - Sehen: Zustand → Logs → Anfragen zeigt bei „Eingang“ „mit Vorrang“ und bei „Sprachausgabe“, wie lange die Sätze in der Reihe warteten und wie viele sie überholten. Journal: vorrang: Stufe 2 überholt N wartende Anfrage(n). /health der Dienste zeigt unter queue Plätze, Wartende und Zähler. - Messen: Zustand → Prüfen → „Vorrang für Sprache“ misst zusätzlich den Fall „Zwei Personen gleichzeitig“: die Sprachausgabe ist mit Sätzen anderer voll (alle Plätze plus zwei Wartende), dann kommt ein Satz einmal normal und einmal mit Vorrang. Gezeigt wird der erste Ton beider Fälle. - Grenzen: Das Sprachmodell (qwen38) selbst kennt keine Reihenfolge: Das Tor wirkt nur auf Anfragen des Panels, Open WebUI und andere Programme, die direkt dorthin fragen, bremst der Vorrang nicht. Spricht nur eine Person, ist nichts schneller.

head: Warum die Installation so aussieht
title: Warum die Installation so aussieht
text: - PyTorch aus dem cu130-Index: Das aarch64-torch auf PyPI hat kein CUDA. Ein einfaches pip install qwen-tts würde also auf der CPU laufen. torch und torchaudio müssen außerdem aus demselben Index kommen, sonst lädt libtorchaudio.so nicht. - Kein flash-attn: Es gibt kein ARM-Wheel, und für sm_121 lässt es sich laut Berichten nicht bauen. Beide Modelle laufen stattdessen mit PyTorch-SDPA. - Getrennte venvs: qwen-asr verlangt transformers==4.57.6, qwen-tts transformers==4.57.3. - ASR mit vLLM: vLLM 0.30 kann Qwen3-ASR selbst, mit /v1/audio/transcriptions, Streaming und mehreren Anfragen gleichzeitig. Es läuft in derselben Umgebung wie die TTS-Engine. qwen-asr[vllm] wird nicht gebraucht (es würde vllm 0.14 erzwingen). - TTS mit vllm-omni: qwen-tts kann nicht stückweise ausgeben. Das Qwen-Team verweist für Streaming auf vllm-omni. vllm 0.30.0 und vllm-omni 0.30.0 haben ARM-Pakete auf PyPI (CUDA 13) und werden nativ in einer eigenen Umgebung installiert, ohne Docker. - Engine-Speicher: vLLM reserviert beim Start einen festen Anteil des *gesamten* Speicherpools, bei TTS pro Stufe (Talker und Code2Wav) getrennt. Die Voreinstellungen (ASR 1.7B 0,06, 0.6B 0,035; TTS 0,04 + 0,025) sind knapp

head: Warum die Installation so aussieht
title: Warum die Installation so aussieht
text: gewählt, damit Speech neben der qwen38-stock-Lane Platz findet. Ist ein Anteil zu klein, bricht die Engine beim Start mit „No available memory for the cache blocks“ ab. Dann im Panel den Anteil erhöhen.

head: Aufbau des Chats
title: Aufbau des Chats
text: Eine Antwort des Assistenten läuft in drei Dateien unter app/panel/:

head: Aufbau des Chats
title: Aufbau des Chats
text: - chat_turn.py (prepare): wer spricht und was er darf (Profil, erkannte Stimme, Geräteschlüssel, Telegram, iPhone-App), der Systemprompt, Antworten auf wartende Vorschläge („Ja“ zu Termin, Mail, Korrektur …), die angebotenen Werkzeuge und die Sperren nach fremdem Text. Ergebnis ist ein Turn mit allen Werten. - chat_tools.py (run): was beim Aufruf eines Werkzeugs passiert (Websuche, Home Assistant, Mail, Kalender, Erinnerungen …). Nur angebotene Werkzeuge laufen, die Sperren werden hier noch einmal geprüft. - chat.py (_answer): fragt das Sprachmodell in Runden, führt Werkzeugaufrufe über chat_tools.run aus, prüft die Antwort und streamt Text und Ton. Werkzeug-Definitionen und Sperrlisten (READS_OUTSIDE, LOCKED_OUTSIDE …) stehen weiter in chat.py.

head: Aufbau des Chats
title: Aufbau des Chats
text: Neue Rechte oder Hinweise gehören nach chat_turn.py, neue Werkzeuge nach chat_tools.py (Definition und Sperrliste in chat.py).

head: Funktionen und Rechte (features.py)
title: Funktionen und Rechte (features.py)
text: Seit V01.0.267 steht jede Funktion, die der Admin schalten kann, genau einmal in app/panel/features.py: Name (de/en), Gruppe, die Admin-Schalter (chat.*), die Funktion, auf der sie aufbaut (parent), der eigene Schalter des Profils (profile), ob Gäste sie je nutzen dürfen, die Ich-Seite und die Anleitung. Gespeichert wird weiter unter den alten Namen in config.json und settings.json; nur diese Tabelle kennt beide.

head: Funktionen und Rechte (features.py)
title: Funktionen und Rechte (features.py)
text: - Eine Prüfung: features.admin_on(key), features.profile_on(key, uid), features.allowed(key, uid) und features.reason(key, uid) (Grund: spark, profile, guest). Die Module fragen nur noch hier (admin_on, usable, allowed sind Einzeiler); was zusätzlich eingerichtet sein muss (Kiwix-Adresse, Agent-Stufe), meldet das Modul über features.READY bzw. features.GRANTED an. - Eine Liste für die Oberfläche: GET /api/features (angemeldet, Rate-Limit) liefert jede Funktion mit Spark an/aus, eigenem Schalter, „darf“ und Grund; Gäste sehen nur Gast-Funktionen. Die Flags in /api/whoami und allow in /api/profile/settings und /api/iphone/settings kommen aus derselben Tabelle. - Neue Funktion: Eintrag in features.py, Anleitung in guides.js. tests/test_features.py wird rot, wenn ein chat.*-Schalter keiner Funktion gehört, ein Profilschalter nicht mit „aus“ beginnt oder ein Modul seine eigene Prüfung baut. - Werte an einer Stelle (seit V01.0.268): common.load_config() füllt jeden fehlenden Schlüssel aus config.default.json (wie jq '.[0] * .[1]' in install.sh); ein zweiter Standardwert im Code (.get(k, anders)) und Handmischungen sind im Selbsttest rot. Was für ein Profil gilt, liefert nur profiles.effe

title: Funktionen und Rechte (features.py)

Am Profil-Shell: body.prof (start.js) zeigt das Admin-Menü nur mit Assistent und Ich; .mainonly sieht der Haupt-Admin, .pwonly nur das Passwort. - App (seit V01.0.272): GET /api/admin/switches liefert zu jedem Schalter names und groups aus features.switch_names(); die App hat keine eigene Liste. title: Live-Übersicht aktuell halten (live.py)

head: Live-Übersicht aktuell halten (live.py)
title: Live-Übersicht aktuell halten (live.py)

B. Wyoming): rec = live.begin(client, gerät), dann rec.step("asr"|"tts", …) und live.end(rec, ok); abgewiesene Absender mit live.door(...). - Etwas, das der Spark von selbst tut (Regel, Erinnerung, Auftrag): live.begin(client, "", uid=…, auto=True, why="festes Wort") und die Schritte darunter mit with live.within(rec): (kein Rückweg zum Gerät). Benachrichtigungen meldet push.send selbst (live.note, Ziele Web Push, Apple Push, Android-App, Telegram); ein neues Tag bekommt ein Wort in push.WHY. - Hintergrundarbeit läuft über vorrang.run/post/in_thread/quiet/hold mit einem festen Namen; das meldet sie selbst an live.bg (kein Inhalt im Namen). - Neue Prüfung am Eingang oder neue Wächter-Stufe: guard.failed und netguard.resolve melden schon selbst an live.refused bzw. live

head: Tests
title: Tests
text: app/tests/ enthält die Selbsttests, die bei jedem Update laufen (cd app && python -m unittest discover -s tests). Alle Dienste sind dabei nachgebaut (tests/helpers.py), kein Test spricht echte Modelle oder Home Assistant an. tests/test_ui_browser.py öffnet das Panel zusätzlich in Chromium (Playwright) am Rechner und in Handybreite: jede Seite ohne Skriptfehler und ohne seitliches Scrollen, die Einstellungssuche, das Ich-Fenster. Ohne Playwright (wie im Selbsttest auf dem Spark) wird er übersprungen; auf GitHub läuft er im Workflow „Tests“ bei jedem Push.

head: Fehlersuche
title: Fehlersuche
text: Die Speicherschätzungen pro Modell (MODEL_GIB in app/common.py) sind grobe Annahmen und noch nicht auf einer Spark gemessen. Nach dem ersten Lauf sollten sie mit den Werten aus dem Panel korrigiert werden.

head: Android app "Spark" (APK, no store)
title: Android app "Spark" (APK, no store)
text: The app is a thin shell around the Spark's page: it shows the Spark as the phone browser does (like the iPhone app, since V01.0.296) and adds only what a page cannot do:

head: Android app "Spark" (APK, no store)
title: Android app "Spark" (APK, no store)
text: - Notes while the app is closed: the app asks the Spark itself every 15 minutes (/api/android/notes), no Google service. Reminders, the morning briefing and notes go there when the app is the device used last or no other way (iPhone app) is set up. - Assistant button: Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant → "Spark"; holding the button opens the app and it listens. - Share to Spark: share text in another app → Spark. The text is put into the text field, you send it yourself. - Emergency stop tile (1.1.0 and later): edit quick settings → add "Notaus". Admins choose "Ganzer Spark" (stage 2) or "Mein Notaus", everyone else "Mein Notaus", always behind a question; lifting only in the browser (see Security and operation). - New version: the app shows a notification when the Spark has a newer APK.

head: Setup
title: Setup
text: 1. Signing key (once, admin): on the Spark (or a Mac) run bash /opt/speech-spark/src/tools/android-schluessel.sh in a terminal (no sudo, needs only openssl). It creates ~/spark-android.p12 and ~/spark-android.pass and shows two values. In the GitHub repo under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → "New repository secret" add both: ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD and ANDROID_KEYSTORE (the long line). Keep both files safe: later versions only install over the old one with the same key. 2. Build the app: Actions → "Android app" → Run workflow. It appears as release android-v1.0.0 with spark.apk, spark.apk.sha256 and android.json. 3. Spark: Settings → Features → Android app on, save, "Fetch the app now" (otherwise it fetches once a day). It checks size and SHA-256 and keeps it under STATE/android. 4. Profile: Me → Android app → "Android app for me" on, "Get a download link", scan the QR code with the Android phone's camera, install the APK (the phone asks once whether the browser may install apps). The link is valid for 30 minutes. 5. In the app: enter the Spark's address (https with a real certificate, e.g. the reverse proxy), sign in with name and PIN like in the browser, allow noti

head: Setup
title: Setup
text: fications and the microphone. For reliable notes turn off battery optimisation for Spark.

head: Security
title: Security
text: - Admin switch chat.android and profile switch android_on, both off; never guests. - The app has no key of its own: it uses its page's login (cookie). Signing out in the page ends it. - The app only loads pages of its own Spark (same address and port), everything else opens in the browser; https only, system certificates. Microphone only for the own Spark page. - #ask= only puts shared text into the text field, nothing is ever sent by itself; both jumps only work in the app. - The APK only comes from GitHub's download addresses with matching size and SHA-256. The download link carries a one-time token (only its hash in memory, 30 minutes, at most 5 downloads); without a valid link 404. - Notes stay in memory only (24 hours, at most 30 per profile) and only go to the profile's own login.

head: New version
title: New version
text: Raise name and code in android/version.properties and push to main: the action builds, signs and publishes android-v<name>; the Spark fetches it and the apps say so.

head: APIs (OpenAI-style)
title: APIs (OpenAI-style)
text: Both services answer GET /health with status and counters. GET /v1/voices (TTS) lists the voices and GET /v1/models the loaded model.

head: APIs (OpenAI-style)
title: APIs (OpenAI-style)
text: Speech recognition accepts anything ffmpeg can read (wav, mp3, webm, mp4, ogg …) and long recordings. language is a code (de) or a name (German); without it the model detects the language. response_format is json, text or verbose_json (with language and duration, without timestamps). With -F stream=true the text arrives in pieces as Server-Sent Events in OpenAI format (transcription.chunk, then [DONE]).

head: Streaming speech
title: Streaming speech
text: With "stream": true (and "response_format": "pcm", the default then) the answer arrives as Server-Sent Events as soon as the first sounds are generated:

head: Streaming speech
title: Streaming speech
text: audio is PCM, 16 bit, mono, 24 kHz. Errors arrive as speech.audio.error. This is vllm-omni's format, passed through unchanged.

head: Streaming speech
title: Steadier delivery
text: Steadier delivery: Qwen samples with temperature 0.9 and top_p 1.0 by default, so tempo and emphasis vary from sentence to sentence. The server therefore applies temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9 and seed 42 (Settings → Speech output). Requests can override them with the same fields, top-level or inside extra_params. In Open WebUI, set response splitting to paragraphs: each part is generated separately, and longer parts sound more coherent. Set the default language to a fixed language instead of auto.

head: Streaming speech
title: Laughing and mood swings
text: Laughing and mood swings: the model reads emojis, "haha", *laughs* and markdown as cues and laughs or changes tone. The server removes them before synthesis (Settings → Speech output → clean text, on by default).

head: Streaming speech
title: Overacting
text: Overacting: exclamation marks and interjections ("Oh", "Wow") make the voice act out excitement. With "speak calmly" (on by default) the server turns "!" into "." and drops such interjections at the start of a sentence. The default voice-chat prompt also asks the LLM for plain, calm everyday language.

head: Streaming speech
title: Numbers
text: Numbers: the server writes numbers out before synthesis, because the model guesses otherwise. Dates, times, money, percent and decimals become words ("on 2026-10-06 at 9:30, $49.90" → "on October sixth, twenty twenty-six at nine thirty, forty-nine dollars ninety"), phone numbers become pairs. Settings → Speech output → reading numbers: as words (default), in pairs, digit by digit or unchanged. Works for German and English.

head: Streaming speech
title: Speaking style
text: Speaking style: "instructions": "calm and friendly, rather slow" in the request. Without it, the default instruction from Settings → Speech output applies. Only the 1.7B models (CustomVoice, VoiceDesign) follow instructions; the 0.6B models ignore them (per the Qwen model card).

head: Streaming speech
title: VoiceDesign
text: VoiceDesign (voice from a description): "task_type": "VoiceDesign" and "instructions": "deep, calm male voice". This needs its own model: enable "VoiceDesign zusätzlich bereitstellen" in Settings → Speech output. It starts a second engine with the same memory footprint again.

head: Streaming speech
title: Streaming speech
text: In the panel under Zustand → Prüfen (Status → Checks), "gestreamt" (streamed) plays audio while it is generated and shows the time to first audio.

head: General
title: General
text: The services behave like the OpenAI audio API: TTS returns mp3 by default (also wav, flac, opus, pcm), STT understands response_format=text, and the language may be an ISO code like de. OpenAI voice names like alloy fall back to the default voice. If an API key is set in the panel, apps must send Authorization: Bearer <key>.

head: Open WebUI
title: Open WebUI
text: If Open WebUI runs in Docker on the same Spark, use the LAN IP or host.docker.internal instead of SPARK (container started with --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway). The panel shows these values ready to copy in the Einbinden tab.

head: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
title: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
text: An agent such as Hermes Agent (Nous Research) or OpenClaw can use the Spark's speech recognition and speech output. The agent runs on another computer and only gets audio and text to read out, no access to the assistant's profiles, memory or tools. The panel shows ready-made snippets under Integrate.

head: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
title: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
text: OpenClaw: tts.provider: "openai" with tts.providers.openai.baseUrl = http://SPARK:31002/v1 (plus apiKey, model, speakerVoice, responseFormat: "mp3"), and for voice messages an entry in tools.media.models with provider: "openai", baseUrl = http://SPARK:31001/v1 and capabilities: ["audio"]; store the key as an OpenAI API key profile.

head: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
title: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
text: Do not install the agent on the Spark itself: it runs commands and could reach settings and keys. Without an API key anyone on the home network can use the speech services.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Spark as an MCP server
text: Other programs use the Spark over the Model Context Protocol (Streamable HTTP, the panel's address /mcp, e.g. http://SPARK:31080/mcp). Off by default.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Switching on
text: Switching on: admin: Features → *Spark as MCP server*. Profile: Me → *Services over MCP* → "Spark as MCP server for me", then "Connect a program with a key": name, tools, "Create key". The key is shown once; enter it in the program as the header Authorization: Bearer <key>.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Rules (fixed, no switch)
text: Rules (fixed, no switch): - Each access belongs to one profile and can only use the tools the profile gave it and may use itself right now. Never to the outside: mail, memory, earlier conversations, secrets, settings. - "Home network only" (default): the key works only for requests straight from the LAN, without proxy headers and not from a listed reverse proxy. - ask_spark: the question counts as outside text. Nothing is switched, saved, learned, sent or proposed; nothing of it lands in the conversations. - Acting: a program only leaves a proposal. The profile gets a notification and decides under Me → Services over MCP ("Yes, do it" with the code window, or "No"). A proposal waits 15 minutes. - Limits: 60 calls per minute and access (ask_spark 10), 2 at once per access, 6 overall; speech runs with the stage "last", people at the Spark go first. Without use an access ends after 90 days. - The journal shows each request as mcp-server: with program, tool and time, never the content. - Status → Live (since V01.0.334) shows each tool call as its own request "MCP-Client" with tool and target (speech as hearing or speaking, a proposal as "Bestätigung anfragen" → push, a confirmed action

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Rules (fixed, no switch)
text: as its own request); the access's name shows only with the profile's consent ("My name in the request log"), contents never. ask_spark shows like a conversation.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: From outside (OAuth)
text: From outside (OAuth): admin: *MCP server from outside* below the switch. An access "from outside" needs the profile's second sign-in step and a fresh code. Programs like claude.ai sign in with OAuth 2.1 (dynamic registration, PKCE S256, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server): add a custom MCP connector with https://your-proxy/mcp in the program, it sends you to the panel, there you see a warning, pick the tools and confirm with your code. Access tokens last 1 hour, refresh tokens 30 days and are swapped with every use. Everything such a program reads goes to its provider.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Examples
text: Examples: Open WebUI: Settings → External tools → "+", type MCP (Streamable HTTP). n8n: node "MCP Client Tool". Programs without a header field: npx mcp-remote http://SPARK:31080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Own MCP services per profile
text: Since V01.0.363 (plan plaene/eigene-mcp-dienste.md) every profile can connect its own MCP services (Streamable HTTP), besides the ones the admin connects for everybody. Only that profile sees and uses them.

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Switching on
text: Switching on: Admin: Features → Agent functions → Services over MCP → *Own MCP services for profiles* (chat.mcp_own), below it *… also in background jobs* (chat.mcp_own_jobs) and *… with sign-in (OAuth)* (chat.mcp_own_oauth); all off. Profile: Me → *My MCP services* → "Own MCP services for me" (mymcp_on), then enter name, address and key and "Connect service". The profile needs no agent level for this.

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Rules (fixed)
text: Rules (fixed): - At most 5 services per profile, each with at most 30 tools. Every tool is "Off" until the profile sets it to "Read" or "Act after yes". If the service changes a tool's description or inputs, it is "Off" again after "Fetch tools again". - Never for guests, never for other profiles, never for a foreign voice at a speaker (only when speech recognition surely heard the profile's own voice), over Telegram only with "private data". - Connecting a service, a new address, a new key: only in the profile's own browser login with a fresh code (second sign-in step, when set up). A new address always needs a new key; all tools are "Off" again then. Keys and sign-in data are kept encrypted (vault), never sent back, never logged. - Connections through the guard (netguard.USER): public addresses with https; home network addresses (also http) only when the admin allows them under Security; the Spark's own services (ports 30000–31099) never. - "Read": the answer is outside text (framed, the assistant switches and saves nothing more in that answer, never learned). "Act after yes": only a proposal; carried out after a plain "Yes" in the next message from the same device and conversati

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Rules (fixed)
text: on, for 15 minutes, never after outside text, never in background jobs, not during Notaus stage 2 or "Mein Notaus". - Limits: 30 seconds per call, at most 2 MB read, 8000 characters to the model, arguments at most 4000 characters, 10 calls per minute and 2 at once per profile. - Background jobs (with the admin switch and the box ticked at the service): reading tools only, only in jobs with private data. - Sign-in (OAuth): if the service wants a sign-in, leave the key empty and tap "Sign in at the service". The Spark reads the service's sign-in addresses (protected resource metadata, authorization server metadata), registers there as a program (dynamic registration, PKCE S256, resource), the browser signs in at the service and comes back through /api/mymcp/back (this address changes nothing, it hands code and state to the signed-in page, 10 minutes, once). Access and refresh token are kept encrypted; the Spark renews the access before it ends.

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Admin
text: Admin: People and devices → Apps and interfaces → *Profiles' own MCP services*: profile, name, address (host only), number of released tools, last fetched, never a key. "Block" applies at once and also when the profile connects the service again; "Remove" deletes it with its key. Optionally a list of allowed hosts (empty: every public one; an entry also allows its subdomains).

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Visible
text: Visible: Status → Live shows each call as a step to the target "MCP-Dienste" and under events "MCP: service · host · ok or error · duration", plus connected, removed, signed in, blocked; never question, arguments or answer, never the profile's name. Me → My status shows one row per service (answers, sign-in needed, blocked). The guard's decisions show under Live as always.

head: "Hey Siri, ask Spark"
title: "Hey Siri, ask Spark"
text: An iPhone shortcut sends the dictated question to POST /api/siri/ask (header X-Speech-Device with a device key of your profile, body {"text": "..."}) and lets Siri speak the answer field. Works without the page open, also on Apple Watch, AirPods and CarPlay; follow-ups within 10 minutes keep the context, and each day's questions are kept as a conversation of the profile. Step by step under Einbinden → Guides.

head: iPhone app "Spark"
title: iPhone app "Spark"
text: Own iPhone app with the Spark voice and "Hey Siri, Frag Spark", paired by QR code, its own key per iPhone that may only ask and listen. Building, pairing and security: iphone-app.md.

head: Messages between profiles (for the iPhone app)
title: Messages between profiles (for the iPhone app)
text: With the profile's browser login or the iPhone app's key (header X-Speech-Device), only when the admin switched on "Messages to others" and the profile "Use messages for me"; other device keys get 403. At most 30 calls a minute. - GET /api/messages: mailbox (items with id, from, name, text, t, read, kind, voice, secs), recipients to, speakers for announcements, switches (all, announce, voice), max_text, max_voice. - GET /api/messages/ready (also while the switches are off): enabled, on, reach (id, name), off (name, why), why; for the ready view. The admin switches every profile on with POST /api/admin/messages/enable_all. - GET /api/messages/poll?since=<ms>: new messages not spoken anywhere yet; marks the device as open (then no notification). - POST /api/messages/played {"id"}: {"play": true} only for the first device that speaks it. - POST /api/messages/send {"to": "<profile id>" | "all", "text"} (at most 500 characters). - POST /api/messages/voice?to=<profile id>: the recording as body (at most 2 MB, 30 seconds); GET /api/messages/audio?id= returns it as Ogg/Opus. - POST /api/messages/announce {"speakers": [id], "text"}, POST /api/messages/read {"ids"?}, POST /api/messages/delet

head: Messages between profiles (for the iPhone app)
title: Messages between profiles (for the iPhone app)
text: e {"ids"?} (without ids: all). - Notifications: APNs with tag msg-<id>, the text comes through /api/iphone/note as before. "Who may write to me" (PUT /api/messages/who) only in the browser. - V01.0.206: to includes call (call name), plus recent (last written to, at most 5) and fav. PUT /api/messages/fav {"id", "on"} sets a favourite (at most 20, also with the app key). PUT /api/messages/call {"call"} sets the own call name (browser only). Admin: GET /api/admin/profiles?q=&show=&sort=&page=&per= (at most 100 per page), GET /api/admin/profiles/<id>, PUT /api/admin/profiles/<id>/call.

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: The watch app "Spark" (app/pebble/speech-spark.pbw, source in pebble/) brings the voice chat to Pebble Time 2 and Core 2 Duo, with the answer as text and through the watch speaker. On Pebble Round 2 the answer is text only. It needs a watch firmware with the speaker API (from about v4.9.170).

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: 1. Pairing with a setup code (new in V01.0.230, off): the admin switches on *Features → Pair the Pebble watch*, the profile "Pebble watch for me" under *Me → Pebble watch*, then "Pair a Pebble" and copy the line (valid 10 minutes, once). The watch gets its own key, which only reaches /api/watch/ and is locked at once by either switch. Without pairing it still works: add a device "Pebble" under Profiles and copy its key. 2. On the paired phone, download http://SPARK:31080/pebble/speech-spark.pbw and open it with the Pebble app. Easier: *Me → Pebble watch* shows a QR code for it to scan with the phone camera. When the Spark has a newer watch app, "Neue Uhr-App" shows under an answer at most once a day; reinstalling keeps the pairing. 3. In the Pebble app, open the settings of "Spark": paste the setup code, or enter the Spark address (http://SPARK:31080) and device key. Settings and "Start App" stay grey while the Pebble app does not see the watch as connected (tab Devices). 4. On the watch: SELECT asks (dictation through the phone), SELECT again stops the speech, long SELECT starts a new conversation. A small face at the top shows whether Spark listens, thinks or speaks; its mouth fo

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: llows the speech. The watch setting Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Volume caps how loud the app can get.

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: The phone must reach the Spark, at home over Wi-Fi, on the road through a VPN such as Tailscale. The app uses HTTP because the Pebble app does not trust the self-signed certificate. On the Spark, POST /api/watch/ask and GET /api/watch/poll serve it: the answer is made like in the voice chat (kept short), the audio is compressed for the small speaker (quiet syllables lifted, peaks softly limited) and goes to the watch as 8 kHz IMA ADPCM. Watch and phone retry lost messages; after 30 s without a message the watch gives up. At the end the phone sends the times to POST /api/watch/report; *Status → Logs* then shows one line watch: zeit … per answer in the area "Watch" (dictation, first text, first sound, done, retries, outcome). The watch shows the same face as the panel (robot or comic), taken over with the next answer.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
title: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
text: The "Spark" app is the iPhone front end for a voice assistant you run yourself on your own computer ("your Spark"). The app only works together with your Spark.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: In short
title: In short
text: - The app talks only to your own Spark. There is no developer server. - The developer receives no data: no usage statistics, no ads, no tracking, no crash reports through own services. - Whoever runs the Spark is responsible for the data stored on it.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: What goes where
title: What goes where
text: The connection to your Spark is encrypted (https). The pairing key is kept in the iPhone's keychain.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: What stays on the iPhone
title: What stays on the iPhone
text: - Wake word: "Hey Spark" is recognised on the iPhone only; nothing goes to Apple or your Spark until you speak. - Camera and photos: the iPhone reads the text itself. Images never leave the iPhone. - Contacts: only to find the number for "Call …". Contacts are not sent to your Spark. - Reminders: after your "yes" the app writes entries into the Reminders app. It reads nothing there for your Spark. - Questions while offline: at most 10 typed questions wait on the iPhone for up to one day.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Notifications through Apple
title: Notifications through Apple
text: If you turn notifications on, your Spark sends only the fixed sentence "Neue Nachricht vom Spark" and a random number through Apple's push service. The iPhone then fetches the actual text directly from your Spark. Apple does not see the content.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Deleting
title: Deleting
text: "Unpair" in the app deletes the pairing key, waiting questions and the reminder mapping on the iPhone. Data on your Spark is deleted in your Spark's panel. Deleting the app removes all of its data from the iPhone.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Contact
title: Contact
text: Questions about the app: https://github.com/db9979/speech-on-dgx-spark/issues

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: The Gespräch tab needs the microphone, and browsers only allow it over https. The panel therefore also listens on https://SPARK:31443 with a self-signed certificate; the browser warns once. The LLM connection is under Settings → Language model (default: qwen38 at http://127.0.0.1:30001/v1). Since V01.0.292 "Model" there offers a choice of the models the server at this address reports (/v1/models, admin only, kept 60 seconds, "Reload" asks at once); "Automatic" takes the first, "Type another …" opens the text field. If the list cannot be read, the text field stays with the reason above it. The installer takes the qwen38 API key from ~/.config/qwen38/api-key of the user who runs sudo ./install.sh. Thinking is off for the chat so the answer starts right away. An animated assistant face shows whether it is listening, thinking or speaking; its mouth follows the voice. The same face sits in the bottom right corner of every tab, so you can talk from anywhere in the panel. Since V01.0.154 the admin picks under Settings → Defaults → "Gesicht des Assistenten" between *Robot* (as before, the default) and *Comic* (a caricature with spiky hair and a short mustache, since V01.0.187 only above th

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: e upper lip). The comic face looks around, blinks with heavy lids, raises its brows, tilts its head, moves mouth and mustache with the voice and shows the state with a coloured ring: grey idle, blue listening, yellow thinking, green speaking, red error. The choice applies to everybody, the iPhone app included; more faces can be added in static/js/face.js. Since V01.0.241 the small picture before each answer in the history shows the chosen face as well. Since V01.0.294 there is a switch "Gesicht zeigt, was es tut" next to it (off): the face then shows a small sign beside the head for what the answer is doing, taken only from the panel's events, never from the model's text: a magnifier for web, document or history searches, a calendar sheet for calendar and briefing, a letter for mail, a light bulb for Home Assistant, a note pad for memory and reminders, thought bubbles while thinking. After an action was done (device switched, something remembered, reminder set) it is pleased for a moment and winks, on an error it looks puzzled with a question mark, and after 5 minutes without conversation or use it falls asleep with "zzz"; a tap, a key or the mouse over the face wake it.

head: Voice chat
title: Start page and password
text: Start page and password: the panel opens with the assistant. Monitoring, settings, voices and logs need the panel password (button "Settings"; the login ends after 7 days without use and renews itself while in use). "Assistant without password" under Settings → Security is off on new installs: then guests are locked out, profiles sign in on the start page with name and PIN (devices with a key keep working), and the admin signs in with "Admin". Switched on, the assistant is open to everyone on the network, also without a profile. The password can be changed under Settings → Security. Scripts can still use HTTP Basic.

head: Voice chat
title: On the phone
text: On the phone: below 760 px the page opens with the big face (tap = talk) and two buttons below it: "Settings" opens the "Ich" window ("Hey Spark" at the top), "History" the messenger view. That view fits the screen exactly: a slim top bar with an arrow back to the face, a small face, state, profile and menu, the history in the middle, and at the bottom a text field and round mic button (a stop button during the answer). The browser remembers which of the two views was open last. The menu (☰) holds new conversation, earlier conversations, conversation settings, language, light/dark and, for admins, every tab.

head: Voice chat
title: Like the app (V01.0.296)
text: Like the app (V01.0.296): on a phone (below 760 px) the page looks like the iPhone app, the same on iPhone and Android. At the bottom are the tabs *Spark* (conversation), *Today* (setup and the same cards and sentences as Me → Today), *Documents*, *Me* and *Manage*; you only see what your role allows (guests only Spark, Manage only with admin rights, Documents only when allowed). Spark shows the face at the top (smaller once there are bubbles), the history below, the big mic button and always the text field; top left "History" (earlier conversations as a sheet from below, swipe down closes) and "New". Me and Manage are lists like the iOS settings; sub-pages slide in from the right, "‹ Back" top left, the Android or Safari back gesture goes exactly one level back. Manage starts with the status, then Features, People and devices, Settings, Logs, Update and backups and Appearance. Under Appearance (Manage or Me) "Show the computer layout" switches back to the old phone view (this browser only); the menu's "Show like the app" returns. It is only another presentation: no new endpoints, the server checks rights as before.

head: Voice chat
title: As an app on your phone
text: As an app on your phone: open https://SPARK:31443 in the phone's browser, accept the certificate warning, then use "Add to Home screen" in the browser menu (iPhone: Safari → Share → "Add to Home Screen"). The assistant then starts full screen with its own icon. With the self-signed certificate Android creates a shortcut instead of an installed app; it works the same, it just does not show up in the app list.

head: Voice chat
title: Better recognition
text: Better recognition: a fixed default language (Settings → Speech recognition, e.g. German) instead of "auto" helps most with short sentences. The "Context" field takes names and terms that are often misheard; the model then prefers them. The 1.7B model is noticeably more accurate than 0.6B and needs about 2–3 GiB more memory.

head: Voice chat
title: Second recognizer: Parakeet
text: Second recognizer: Parakeet. Under Settings → Speech recognition → "Recognizer" the admin switches between Qwen3-ASR (GPU) and Parakeet (primeline/parakeet-primeline, a German fine-tune of NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3; the download is flozen1981/parakeet-primeline-onnx, an int8 ONNX export of it, run via sherpa-onnx; idea from winidi/dictate). Parakeet runs on the CPU and needs about 1 GiB; the Qwen3-ASR engine is stopped meanwhile. It ignores the context field, and a stream returns the whole text in one piece. The first start downloads about 640 MB.

head: Voice chat
title: Conversation comfort
text: Conversation comfort: the assistant knows the date and time (the browser's time zone; can be turned off under Settings → Language model). Conversations are kept in the browser and can be reopened or deleted at the top of the conversation. With "live transcript" the text appears while you speak; in the pause the recognition is usually already done, so that step is skipped at the end.

head: Voice chat
title: Guides
text: Guides: every service that can be switched on has an openable guide (what it does, what you need, setup, example phrases, what leaves the house, switching off, troubleshooting): next to its switch under Features, at the top of its page in the "Ich" window and collected under Features → Guides. Services are sorted into the same groups everywhere: Conversation, My day, Mail and documents, Home, On the go and devices, Security and access. The texts live in app/panel/static/js/guides.js; a self-test checks that no switch is left without a guide and group.

head: Voice chat
title: Weather, contacts, parcels (V01.0.93)
text: Weather, contacts, parcels (V01.0.93): three small services, each off by default, allowed by the admin under Features and switched on by each profile itself in the "Ich" window; never guests. *Weather* comes straight from Open-Meteo (no key, only the place's coordinates leave, own address configurable); the Spark builds fixed sentences from the numbers, also for the daily briefing and the proactive weather note. *Contacts* reads an address book over CardDAV (iCloud: https://contacts.icloud.com with an app-specific password, Nextcloud, others) once a day and keeps it encrypted: phone numbers, e-mail addresses, birthdays (in the briefing and as a notice), names instead of addresses in mail. Contact text counts as outside text. *Parcels* recognises shipping mails of DHL, Hermes, DPD, GLS, UPS and Amazon in the profile's own mailbox (14 days) and says what comes today, is on its way, waits for pick-up or was delivered; no carrier is asked, parcel lines count as mail text.

head: Voice chat
title: Telegram (V01.0.96)
text: Telegram (V01.0.96): your own bot from @BotFather (guide in the panel). The admin switches it on under Features and enters the token (stored encrypted); the Spark asks Telegram for new messages itself, no open port needed. Each profile links its Telegram in the "Ich" window with a one-time code (10 minutes) and writes or sends voice messages (speech recognition on the Spark). Strangers get one fixed sentence, groups nothing. Per profile, all off at first: answers also as voice messages, notifications over Telegram, personal data (calendar, mail, contacts, parcels, documents; also appointments and mail in notifications) and switching the smart home, only with the code word. Commands: /neu, /stimme, /trennen.

head: Voice chat
title: Own speakers (ESP32, V01.0.99, without display since V01.0.104)
text: Own speakers (ESP32, V01.0.99, without display since V01.0.104): small ESP32-S3 boards (16 MB flash, PSRAM, INMP441 microphone, MAX98357A amplifier, e.g. the XiaoZhi breadboard boards) become a voice assistant in the room. Firmware: the open XiaoZhi firmware at a fixed version, German, wake word "Jarvis", without a built-in cloud address; a GitHub Action (.github/workflows/firmware.yml, settings in firmware/xiaozhi.json) builds it as release fw-<version>. The Spark fetches the newest one daily (or on a button), checks every file against manifest.json and keeps it with the previous one. Set up in the "Ich" window → Speakers: over USB from Chrome or Edge (Web Serial, esptool-js 0.5.7 ships with the panel) the browser writes firmware and a settings block (Wi-Fi, Spark address, device key); the Wi-Fi password never reaches the Spark. Without a PC a board shows or says a 6-digit code. Each speaker is a device key of its profile (voice, memory, smart home with code word, room). Updates arrive over Wi-Fi when the board starts (per device "auto" can be switched off) or over USB. Admin switch chat.esp32 and profile switch, both off at first; the reverse proxy must pass WebSockets. Board var

head: Voice chat
title: Own speakers (ESP32, V01.0.99, without display since V01.0.104)
text: iants: no display, OLED 128×32, OLED 128×64, colour display, since V01.0.133 the Waveshare ESP32-S3-AUDIO-Board (round board with ES8311 audio chip and two microphones; display and camera are optional there). When a board is rewritten over USB with another variant, updates follow the board type it reports at start; the no-display variant never touches the display pins and, since firmware 2.5.1.3 (V01.0.132), no longer loads font and emoji either, which made it crash right after joining the Wi-Fi. Start check only by POST of at most 16 KB, at most 3 open codes per address, firmware only from github.com downloads with a size limit.

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131): under Me → Speakers every speaker has a *Check* button. It shows whether the admin and profile switches are on, whether there is firmware for the board variant, whether the board ever checked in, which address is in the board (with a warning for https://<IP> or port 31443, whose self-signed certificate the board refuses, for localhost and for a missing address) and what the speaker did lately: start check, connection, refused connection with its reason, wake word, microphone (length, loudest moment and mean in dB, whether there was speech), what was understood and how much sound went back. These lines stay in memory only (40 per speaker, gone when the panel restarts). *Check network* asks the address from the Spark the way the board does: GET /api/esp32/ping (answers with a marker of this Spark) and a WebSocket with x-spark-probe: 1; this shows whether the address leads to this Spark, whether the certificate is accepted, whether the reverse proxy redirects or blocks WebSockets. Allowed like Home Assistant (home network yes, the Spark's own service ports no), only these two paths, answers of at most 4 KB, six checks in ten minutes per profile. Behind

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: a router without NAT loopback the check can fail although the board reaches the Spark. *Test: sound and microphone* plays the soft tone and a test sentence at the next "Jarvis" or button press (at once when connected) and then checks the microphone with the next sentence: the speaker says what it understood, or that it heard nothing. *Read the board's log (USB)* connects the board in Chrome or Edge, restarts it and reads for 45 seconds what the firmware reports; the page translates the known lines (Wi-Fi joined or not, certificate refused, Spark unreachable, status 403, pairing code, conversation connection, crash, brownout, sound error). The text stays in the browser, words like token or password are blacked out; *Copy* takes it along for a bug report. Since V01.0.136 the list under *Check* follows live (every 2 seconds while the page is visible); in room mode it only says that a sentence was heard and whether it speaks in a pause, never what was heard. Since V01.0.135 every speaker has a *Volume* slider under Me → Speakers (0 to 100; the Spark sends it at every connection through the firmware's MCP tool self.audio_speaker.set_volume, at once when connected) and a *Microphone* cho

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: ice less sensitive / normal / more sensitive (from which level the Spark takes sound as speech: about −41, −47 or −53 dB). Since V01.0.134 a quiet level from about −47 dB (and three times above the background noise) counts as speech, quiet recordings are raised up to 20 times before speech recognition, and every question writes a line "esp32: microphone at …" with length and level to the log. The log now also shows the start checks ("esp32: start check from …") and the reason of every refused connection. Since V01.0.137 the Spark buffers the sound: it starts only when 0.6 seconds are ready, keeps at most 0.9 seconds in flight (since V01.0.138: 0.7) (the board holds 1.2 seconds) and after a stall collects 0.3 seconds again instead of sending single snippets. When speech output could not keep up, *Check* shows "Ton stockte N-mal" and the log "esp32: sound stalled"; if it stutters without that line, the board's Wi-Fi is the cause. Since V01.0.138 (firmware 2.5.1.5) the board no longer drops sound when its buffer is full but waits; the connection then slows the Spark down. Before, Wi-Fi delays added up in long answers, the buffer overflowed and the gaps grew towards the end. The Spark'

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: s lead is lowered to 0.7 seconds so old firmware has more room too. The board fetches the new firmware itself at its next start (unplug it briefly).

head: Voice chat
title: Speaker page (V01.0.149)
text: Speaker page (V01.0.149): Me → Speakers shows the switch "Own speakers for me" at the top, then "My speakers" (one line per speaker with its state: connected, room mode until, update available) and "Add a speaker" with two ways: *Set up a new board over USB* (Chrome/Edge on a PC) and *Board shows a code*. Tapping a speaker opens its page in sections: Sound (volume, microphone), Room mode ("Listen now" as a Start/Stop button, duration, how much it may say, *What it may offer* with the same seven kinds as in the browser, stored per speaker on the Spark, room in Home Assistant, detect more, and with "Ignore TV voices" also who it listens to and trial), Voice (teach "My voice through this speaker"), Firmware (version, update now, updates by themselves, rewrite the firmware over USB), Check (checks with a readable board name, check network, sound and microphone test, live recent events, board log over USB) and *Remove speaker* at the bottom. Admin: under Features → Own speakers the firmware state comes first, then the address with *Check address* (tried from the Spark like "Check network", admin only, at most 6 checks in 10 minutes). Under People and devices and Me → Security speaker ke

head: Voice chat
title: Speaker page (V01.0.149)
text: ys are marked "Speaker, managed under Me → Speakers"; they cannot be moved to another profile.

head: Voice chat
title: Tasks and shopping list (V01.0.96)
text: Tasks and shopping list (V01.0.96): "Put milk on the shopping list", "What is on my to-do list?". Admin switch and profile switch, both off at first. Each of the two lists lives either on the Spark, where an iPhone shortcut with the device key fetches new entries (POST /api/tasks/inbox?list=einkauf, header X-Speech-Device; a GET only reads and changes nothing) into the Reminders app, or in a CalDAV task list of a calendar account (Nextcloud, mailbox.org, Radicale). Adding happens at once, ticking off and deleting by voice only after "Yes". After outside text the assistant adds nothing in the same answer.

head: Voice chat
title: Bus and train (V01.0.102)
text: Bus and train (V01.0.102): "When does the next bus leave?", "How do I get to Karlsruhe at 8?". Admin switch and profile switch, both off at first. Timetable from transport.rest (default https://v6.db.transport.rest, own address configurable); fixed sentences with delay, platform and cancellations. With a commute (destination, time, days) "Proactive" speaks up 45 to 5 minutes before when the connection is 5 or more minutes late or cancelled. Timetable text counts as outside text.

head: Voice chat
title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: Agent functions (V01.0.175): the assistant works longer for you. Admin: Features → "Agent functions" on and pick a level per profile: *off* (default), *read and report only* or *also act after "Yes"*. The profile then switches it on itself under Me → Jobs. Never guests, other voices or ESP32 speakers. - *Background jobs:* "Research which heat pump fits the pool and let me know." The job runs in the background (search, read pages, with "my data" also appointments, reminders and documents), then a notification comes by browser, iPhone app and Telegram (as set under Me → Notifications). The full report is under Me → Jobs and in the log, on request as a document under "My documents" (switch "Also keep every report under "Documents"" or "As document" at the job). Limits: one job at a time on the Spark, it waits while someone talks to the assistant; 8 rounds, 4 searches, 5 pages, 12 tool calls, 15 minutes, 20,000 characters; 3 waiting and 20 jobs per day and profile. A job only has reading tools, its report counts as outside text and is never learned. - *Scheduled jobs:* "Sum up my appointments of the week every Monday at 7." The assistant reads the plan back in fixed words, it is saved

title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: only after your "Yes". Once, daily, weekdays, weekly or monthly, at most 10, pause and delete under Me → Jobs. If the Spark was off for more than 3 hours at the planned time, that run is skipped. - *Routines (level "also act" only):* "Remember as routine Evening: terrace light on, pool to 36 degrees." After "Yes", later "Evening" is enough. Every step is a Home Assistant sentence and runs like a spoken command (same allowlist, same code word); at most 8 steps and 20 routines. - *Services over MCP:* below "Agent functions" the switch "Services over MCP". The admin enters name, address (Streamable HTTP) and token (login plus a fresh code; token in the vault, never sent back). Every tool is off until the admin sets it to "read" or "act", and the profiles are ticked per service. Reading answers count as outside text; acting tools only propose and run after the "Yes". If a service changes a tool's description or inputs, it is off again after "Fetch tools again". The Spark never starts a program itself; home network addresses only with the permission under Security. - *Own MCP services (V01.0.363):* below "Services over MCP" the switch "Own MCP services for profiles". Every profile conne

head: Voice chat
title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: cts up to five services of its own under Me → My MCP services (fresh code, key encrypted) and releases every tool itself ("Read" or "Act after yes"). Optionally in background jobs (read only) and with sign-in (OAuth). The admin sees all of them under Apps and interfaces and can block each at once. Details: APIs and integration.

head: Voice chat
title: Messages to others (V01.0.192)
text: Messages to others (V01.0.192): profiles of the same Spark send each other short messages. Admin: Features → "Messages to others" (off), below it separately "Message to everybody", "Announcements on speakers" and "Voice messages" (all off). Profile: Me → Messages → "Use messages for me" (off). There you also set who may write (every profile with messages or only picked ones), who is blocked, whether messages to everybody arrive, what your own speakers say (nothing, only who wrote, with the text) and whether others may announce on them. Guests can neither send nor receive. When you ask in a conversation to write to someone, an earlier answer from web, mail or an image is left out for this, so the tool can be offered (V01.0.196). When sending is not possible (switch off, guest, Telegram without "private"), the assistant names exactly that reason. Simpler (V01.0.200): beside the input field in the assistant (on a phone "Message" below) the envelope opens one line: pick the recipient, type, send. The language model is not involved, earlier answers from web or mail lock nothing. When you say "Schreib sb, dass ich später komme", "Sag Anna, das Essen ist fertig" or "Nachricht an Ben: …",

head: Voice chat
title: Messages to others (V01.0.192)
text: the panel reads recipient and text itself (fixed rules), reads the message back and sends after "Ja". When messages are still off for you, the assistant asks whether to switch them on; your "Ja" switches on only your own profile and then goes on to the message. When sending is not possible it names the reason (admin switch off, "sb has messages off" …). Under Me → Messages "Ready" shows what is on and who can be reached; there and under Features the admin can "Switch on for every profile" (each profile can switch it off again).

head: Voice chat
title: Many profiles (V01.0.206)
text: Many profiles (V01.0.206): under People and devices the admin searches by name, call name or device, filters (not used for 90 days, without a device, with/without second step, messages on/off), sorts (name, last used, newest) and pages through 25 at a time. "Details" shows each profile's devices, last use, call name, change PIN, reset second step and delete; deleting now needs the fresh code like changing the PIN. The device list shows only the devices of the profiles shown,. Since V01.0.257 the profile of an own device key (script, shortcut) and of a new device is picked from a list of all profiles instead of typing a name; the iPhone app, speakers, Pebble watch and Home Assistant keys are set up by each profile itself under Me, show "🔒 fixed" with where they are managed, and can only be deleted here (the server refuses moving them too). "Last used" counts the browser login (without the address) and device keys. Call name: optional per profile ("Tom", "Dad"), set by the admin in the details or by the profile under Me → Messages; unique among all names and call names. Picking the recipient: in the envelope and under Me → Messages a field "To …": typing shows at most 8 matching prof

text: iles, empty shows ★ favourites (at most 20) and the last ones written to (5). With many profiles "Ready" shows only the number, the names open with a search. Same names: when several profiles fit the spoken name (two "Thomas"), the assistant asks "Thomas Müller or Thomas Meier?" (at most 4); the answer ("Müller", "the first", call name) picks only among these, then comes the usual "Ja". When more than 4 fit it asks for the full name. An unknown name gets at most 3 similar ones, never the whole list. "To everybody" names at most 4 and "and N more". - Sending: "Tell Anna dinner is ready." The panel finds the recipient itself among the profiles that take messages from you, reads the message back and sends it only after a plain "Yes" on the same device. Or pick the recipient under Me → Messages and type. "Tell everybody …" goes to all that take messages to everybody. - Arriving, once: when a page of the recipient is open, it speaks the message; else an own connected speaker (if wanted); else one notification on the device used last (browser, iPhone app, Telegram only with personal data allowed). A speaker says messages nobody heard yet from the last two hours at its next wake word. Spe

head: Voice chat
title: Many profiles (V01.0.206)
text: akers never talk during quiet hours. - Reading and replying: "Do I have messages?", then "Reply to her: coming" and "Yes". What a message says counts as outside text: it is only reported, locks everything that changes something for the rest of the answer and the next turn, and never goes into the memory. The panel takes the reply from your own words. - Announcement: "Announcement in the living room: dinner is ready" (or "everywhere"), after "Yes". A tone, then "Durchsage von …"; when the speaker is not connected, at its next wake word within ten minutes. - Voice message: Me → Messages → "Record" (at most 30 seconds), "Send". The speech recognition adds the text; it plays under Me → Messages or on the open page. - Limits: 500 characters, 30 messages an hour, 10 to the same person, 5 to everybody or announcements; 100 messages in the mailbox, deleted after 30 days. Text and recordings are stored encrypted on the Spark, never in the journal (only length and profile), and are not in backups.

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant Assist over Wyoming (V01.0.100)
text: Home Assistant Assist over Wyoming (V01.0.100): Home Assistant uses the Spark's speech recognition and voice (Voice PE, HA app, ESPHome speakers). Admin: Features → "Home Assistant Assist (Wyoming)" on and enter Home Assistant's address (Wyoming has no password; with no address listed the Spark answers nobody). Since V01.0.106 the field suggests the address from a profile's Home Assistant setup when switched on (home network addresses only; behind a reverse proxy enter the real HA address by hand) and shows addresses refused lately. In HA: integration "Wyoming Protocol", host = the Spark, port 31003; in the voice assistant pick "spark" for speech-to-text and text-to-speech. The service runs inside the panel, so it needs the full install. Since V01.0.334 Status → Live shows every transcription and every spoken answer for Home Assistant as a request of the device "Home Assistant" (way Hearing → text to Home Assistant, or Speaking → back), refused senders under Entrance; never the words.

head: Voice chat
title: Weather place
text: Weather place: postcode and place ("76307 Karlsbad") work; the name is searched in Germany and the postcode compared. When several places fit, the others can be picked; coordinates ("48.87, 8.50") work too.

head: Voice chat
title: Web search
text: Web search: switch on "Websuche" under Features and enter the address of your SearXNG instance right below it. If SearXNG's settings.yml allows json under search: formats:, the panel uses the JSON API, otherwise it reads the normal results page; "Test connection" shows whether it works. The LLM then searches by itself when a question needs current information (the LLM server needs tool calling; qwen38 has it on). The assistant says it is looking it up, reads the top pages and shows the sources under the answer. Since V01.0.130 the search is never silently missing: when it is off or has no address, the assistant says so, and the log has a line "chat: web search …" for every question (offered, off, no address, locked). Asking in so many words ("such im Internet", "google mal", "recherchier", "schau online nach", "search the web") always goes through the search. After reading a mail the search stays locked for the rest of that answer (a mail could otherwise carry its content to the web). Since V01.0.194 an answer from mail (also a mail note the assistant made by itself) stays in the next turn only when the new question is about it ("what else does she write?", "read the first one"); t

title: Web search
text: hen the search stays locked and the assistant says so. Any other question ("what is going on in politics today?") leaves the mail answer out and searches.

head: Voice chat
title: Wake word "Hey Spark"
text: Wake word "Hey Spark": with the checkbox below the chat the assistant keeps listening. Say "Hey Spark" and it listens; "Hey Spark, what's the weather?" in one go is taken as the question. The browser detects speech bursts, the speech recognition on the Spark checks for the phrase, nothing goes to the internet. The screen stays on; on a phone keep the app in the foreground.

head: Voice chat
title: The "Ich" (me) window
text: The "Ich" (me) window: since V01.0.125 in the same groups as the Features page (conversation, my data, my day, mail and contacts, home, on the go and devices, access); on a computer it starts with an *Overview* (the state of each page, e.g. "2 calendars connected"), on a phone the state sits right below each entry of the list. Notifications and the daily briefing have their own page *Notifications*. the button with your name (or "Guest") at the top of the history and the settings icon below the face open the same window. On the left is a short list: Conversation and, logged in, Memory, Log and Security, plus, depending on the features switched on, Documents, Calendar, E-mail, Smart home, Voice, Von selbst (speaking up by itself) and Raum-Modus (room mode); as a guest it shows "Sign in". Conversation holds listening (stop on silence, live transcript, barge-in and its sensitivity), answer (voice, profiles only; speaking rate, answer length) and display. Guests always hear the default voice. Logged in, the settings live in the profile on the Spark and apply on every device, including speakers with a device key; as a guest only in the browser. "Hey Spark" is set per device because it k

head: Voice chat
title: The "Ich" (me) window
text: eeps the microphone and screen awake. Defaults for guests and new profiles are under Settings → Defaults. The speaking rate keeps the pitch; it also works for other apps that send speed to the TTS API (vllm-omni backend).

head: Voice chat
title: Own documents
text: Own documents: logged-in profiles upload their own files in the "Ich" window (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, text, Markdown, HTML, CSV, e-mail as .eml; up to 20 MB each, at most 200 per profile). When asked about them, the assistant searches them and names the document with its page below the answer. Guests cannot upload anything, and no profile sees another's documents. Can be turned off under Features.

head: Voice chat
title: Knowledge from uploads (V01.0.224, plan `plaene/wissen-aus-uploads.md`)
text: Knowledge from uploads (V01.0.224, plan plaene/wissen-aus-uploads.md): a profile's documents now live in one SQLite file users/<profile>/wissen.db (documents, text pieces, FTS5 full-text index over the same rough word stems as before, meaning vectors, pages still to be read). Older documents (docs/<id>.json) are taken over the first time they are opened, also after restoring an old backup. The backup copies the file with SQLite's backup function, so it is complete even while being written. Under Me → Documents "View" shows a document's stored text with its pages (and a kept original: pictures and PDFs in the browser, everything else only as a download), every document has a switch "the assistant searches it", "Try the search" shows the hits without the language model, and the sources below an answer can be clicked. Three switches below "Own documents", each off by default, the admin under Features and the profile under Me → Documents (admin defaults never switch them on, never guests): - *Read pictures and scans:* photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP) and PDF pages without text (the page's biggest picture) are cleaned like chat pictures (format check, at most 40 megapixels, upright, 1600 pixels

title: Knowledge from uploads (V01.0.224, plan `plaene/wissen-aus-uploads.md`)
text: , no location or camera data) and wait in the database. The language model reads one page after another and briefly describes what it shows, with no tools and only after a minute without anyone talking to the assistant (wissen.quiet(), where the speech priority rule hooks in); at most 30 pages per document, 200 waiting pages and 100 pages read per profile and day, two tries per page. head: Voice chat
title: Knowledge from uploads (V01.0.224, plan `plaene/wissen-aus-uploads.md`)
text: kages: onnxruntime 1.22.1, tokenizers 0.22.1. - *Keep originals:* the file stays under users/<profile>/docs/files/ (pictures cleaned), up to the space per profile (chat.doc_quota_mb, 50 to 5000, default 500); when it is full only the text is kept. Opening works only as a download (Content-Disposition: attachment, HTML as application/octet-stream), never as a page of the panel.
